items.stem: Who alone saw Oedipus' passing?
options: Theseus
Antigone
Ismene
The messenger

items.stem: What one word, Oedipus says, wipes out his daughters' burdens?
options: Love
Duty
Honour
Fate

items.stem: Complete the line: “Wipes out all score of _____—love.”
options: victories
honours
tribulations
secrets

items.stem: Complete the line: “The pact of Theseus and _____.”
options: Creon
Polyneices
Peirithous
Laius

items.stem: How does the messenger describe the end?
options: Without pain, most marvellous
Violent and cruel in every part
Unknown even to Theseus himself
A death already suffered in open battle

items.stem: Where does Antigone decide to go?
options: Back to Thebes
On to Corinth
Up to Delphi
To remain in Athens forever

items.stem: Why does the Messenger say the teller is content to be counted a fool?
options: Because the tale of the end may seem foolishness to some
Because he has already forgotten what Theseus asked him to say
Because the daughters have already forbidden him to speak at all
Because the chorus has already called the news a lie outright

items.stem: What does Theseus refuse the daughters?
options: To show them the grave
Food and a place of shelter
His protection in the land
A guard to see them home

items.stem: What does the Chorus say as the play closes?
options: Wail no more; all is ordered for the best
Leave the land before the sun has set
Call the messenger back to tell the tale again
Keep watch beside the hidden place all night

items.stem: Complete the line: “The hair of all stood up and all were _____;”
options: angered
silenced
honoured
’mazed

items.stem: Complete the line: “That time and friendship prompt in their _____.”
options: behoof
absence
anger
silence

items.stem: Why must the others leave before the end, according to the reported charge?
options: So that only Theseus stays to behold what may not lawfully be seen or heard
So that the daughters can already begin the long journey home alone now
So that the messenger can hide the king from every later visitor here
So that the chorus can finish a rite already started at the altar there this hour

items.stem: Who calls Oedipus by name and says that his passing has been delayed too long?
options: A voice that summoned him, speaking as the call of the god
Theseus, already waiting at the basin to lead him down the path
The messenger, already bidding the daughters to depart at once
The chorus, already ending the prayer of the last ode here

items.stem: Which convention is at work when the end is reported by a messenger, and only one living witness is said to know the doom?
options: Offstage action reported by a messenger
A comic close that jokes about the hidden doom
A satire of the city's rites in this last scene
Dramatic irony about who may know the doom

items.stem: What does Theseus swear, just before the end, when Oedipus asks him to take the daughters' hands?
options: To be their constant friend, and not to forsake them
To show them the hidden place as soon as he is gone now
To send them at once against a neighbouring city today
To leave the grove before the messenger can speak at all

items.stem: Complete the line: “That sight _____?”
options: ordinary
forgotten
ineffable
distant

items.stem: Complete the line: “His end was _____; therefore, children, stay”
options: bitter
sudden
hidden
blessèd

items.stem: Near which marks does the messenger place the basin and the abrupt, earth-rooted threshold?
options: The Thorician rock, a hollow pear-tree, and a marble tomb along the path
A new grave already hidden from every later visitor in the whole city
The altar of Poseidon, where the last ode had called the king himself
A battlefield already named for the war of the two brothers now in the field

items.stem: How does Antigone first answer the chorus when they ask if Oedipus is then gone?
options: All is but surmise; then gone, reft from sight, not by battle or sea storm
She has already seen the hidden place and can describe it in full now
The messenger has invented the whole tale only to frighten them here
Theseus has already promised to show them the grave at once today for them

items.stem: Which literary element names the feeling of the close, when the chorus bids the mourners wail no more and says that all is ordered for the best?
options: Tone
Comedy
Satire
Plot

items.stem: Complete the line: “It thundered from the _____; the maids”
options: city-wall
harbour
netherworld
marketplace

items.stem: Complete the line: “Of _____ tells they come this way.”
options: lamentation
triumph
silence
rumour

items.stem: How does the charge about the hidden tomb, as Theseus reports it, serve the city?
options: If he keeps the hest, he shall hold his realm at rest, a promise pledged to Zeus
If he shows the place, the daughters will already have won the war at home now
If he hides the messenger, no later visitor will ever learn the whole tale
If he leaves the grove, the chorus will already have ended every remaining rite today

items.stem: How should we read Antigone's cry “Lead me thither; slay me there”, together with what follows in the scene?
options: As a cry of grief, which the chorus answers with refuge
As a legal demand that Theseus must lead her to the hidden place at once
As a report that she has already been killed beside the hidden place itself
As a comic aside, which the chorus treats as a joke about the whole journey home

items.stem: What is the force of Antigone's saying that the sight was ineffable, and that all is but surmise?
options: She marks the end as something witnessed only in part, which words cannot finish telling
She claims she has already stood inside the hidden place and can describe it fully now
She accuses the messenger of having invented every part of the tale himself
She asks Theseus to repeat the unspeakable sights for the chorus at once here today

items.stem: Which reading best holds together the painless end, the hidden tomb, and the chorus's last word?
options: A god-sent end, kept in trust by Theseus, after which the civic voice bids the mourners rest
A battlefield death, already shown on stage, after which Athens refuses the daughters any care at all now
A comic close that treats the daughters' grief as a passing joke about the sacred grove
A claim that the messenger has already opened the hidden tomb to the whole city
